research_question: Under identical inputs, anchor U_s and current per-channel gate G (plan P1/P4), does relaxing the linear correction basis from Q1's structured A=W1^T diag(alpha) W2^T to a fully free A_Q1+D improve source-out gated increment error, versus the competing explanations of Q1 basis restriction, insufficient calibration coverage / distribution proximity, or genuine finite-increment state dependence? Screening only: 80-site cheap landscape + 6 expensive sites + conditional high/0; zero new video/reference/benchmark.

hypotheses_with_opposing_predictions.prediction: Q1's structured basis is genuinely too restrictive: FREE_RIDGE main (lambda=1e-3) DEV5 source-equal-weight gated math MSE is below Q1 by more than epsilon_num=1e-6 at one or more expensive sites, the paired gain survives the stronger robustness lambda=1e-2, D exercises directions beyond the Q1 structured span (training numerical rank), and the gain is visible in the deployed BF16 cache/gate replay as well as the FP32 math lift.
hypotheses_with_opposing_predictions.discriminator: dev5_paired_vs_q1 (ridge_math_sse and ridge_replay_sse) + robust-lambda stability (ridge_robust_info) + D_numerical_rank/gram_numerical_rank + math-lift vs BF16-replay separation, benchmarked against the ICC svd_r512 two-residual nonlinear low-rank control and reuse-Y.

hypotheses_with_opposing_predictions.prediction: Any apparent FREE_RIDGE source-out gain is an artifact of calibration coverage / homogeneous-cohort distribution proximity or ridge overfitting of ~500 severely underdetermined CAL rows (or reflects genuine finite-increment state dependence), NOT a real basis restriction: the DEV5 gain collapses under robust lambda=1e-2, or omega_dev is high (DEV DeltaU lies largely outside the CAL training row space) so the 'source-out' gain is subspace interpolation, or the gain appears only in FP32 math lift and vanishes/reverses in BF16 replay, or the ICC nonlinear control matches/exceeds the free linear arm.
hypotheses_with_opposing_predictions.discriminator: omega_dev per DEV source + ridge_normal_residual + D_numerical_rank + robust-lambda collapse + math-vs-replay divergence + ICC_zero_increment_control and ICC vs FREE_RIDGE ordering; CAL4 provenance (already used for the original Q1 fit) and DEV5 EXPOSED_DEVELOPMENT (not blind) labels.

adversarial_counterexample: Concrete scenario that would overturn the main mechanism claim: the chip10 cohort is homogeneous (similar 'chip' scenes with correlated subject/camera motion), so CAL4 and DEV5 share a low-dimensional dominant DeltaU row subspace. The free D is fit on only ~114-137 matched rows/source (~500 CAL rows) for a 5120x5120 matrix, so M=Sum X_c^T X_c has numerical rank ~<=500 << 5120 and D is determined by data only inside that CAL row space (ridge drives D->0 in the null space, i.e. A_free->A_Q1 there). If DEV5 DeltaU lies mostly INSIDE this shared subspace (omega_dev LOW), a CAL-row-space correction that overfits CAL-specific residual structure (including BF16 quantization/sampling aliasing of the 2048-row uniform panel intersection) will transfer to DEV5 and reduce small-M paired gated MSE -- yet the true full-M linear operator may be no better than Q1. The conclusion 'linear basis restriction matters' would then be WRONG: the gain is distribution proximity + ridge overfit within a shared subspace, not evidence that Q1's structured span was the binding constraint. A second variant: the gain exists only in the FP32 math lift and disappears in the deployed BF16 cache/gate replay, meaning D is fitting sub-quantization noise rather than functional curvature. Readouts in THIS design that would expose it: (1) omega_dev -- if low, the DEV5 'source-out' gain is interpolation, not extrapolation, and cannot separate basis restriction from coverage; (2) robust lambda=1e-2 -- if the DEV5 gain collapses, it was a regularization/overfit artifact; (3) D_numerical_rank/gram_numerical_rank -- reveals how few directions are actually data-identified; (4) math-lift vs BF16-replay separate tables -- exposes sub-rounding noise fitting; (5) increment-normalized vs full-Y-normalized auxiliary -- exposes small-increment-denominator inflation; (6) ICC nonlinear low-rank control and reuse-Y baseline. The design honestly bounds the claim (DEV5 EXPOSED_DEVELOPMENT not blind; CAL4 already used for Q1; no full-M residual writeback; ridge uniqueness != identification), so the mechanism conclusion must remain 'development screening evidence', never 'basis restriction proven'. Full discrimination requires the deferred R2 blind/shared capture and R3 full-M writeback.

findings.item: fit_core.py free_ridge_fit normal-equation residual diagnostic (line 121) uses the wrong gate orientation: lhs = (m.double() * g2[None,:]) @ d64 + ridge*d64 computes M.G^2.D, but the correct normal equation satisfied by the eigen solve (and by the per-column dense reference) is M.D.G^2 + ridge.D = B.G^2 (gate scales OUTPUT columns on the RIGHT). It must be lhs = (m.double() @ d64) * g2[None,:] + ridge*d64. Consequence (a): selfcheck.py line 34 raises RuntimeError('ridge normal residual too large') because the buggy residual exceeds 1e-4 for its non-uniform synthetic gate g=rand(5)+0.5; runner_screen.run() calls selfcheck_run() at line 132 BEFORE any pass, so the guarded job aborts at selfcheck and produces NO screening results. Consequence (b): the predeclared identification metric ridge_normal_residual would be reported as a large bogus value (~0.3), falsely signaling solve failure. The actual ridge SOLVE (shared-Gram eigh + column filter) is correct; only this residual diagnostic is wrong. One-line fix, but it blocks execution and corrupts a pre-registered readout.
findings.evidence: Independent pure-JS replication of the fit (d=5, n=7, S=2, non-uniform per-channel g in [0.5,1.5], lam=1e-2, D solved per-column by dense F64-equivalent elimination): CORRECT residual ||M D G^2 + ridge D - B G^2||/||B G^2|| = 1.175e-16 (machine precision); CODE-formula residual ||M G^2 D + ridge D - B G^2||/||B G^2|| = 3.431e-1 >> selfcheck threshold 1e-4. Derivation: gated source-equal-weight loss column j gives (g_j^2 M + lam/ZA I) d_j = g_j^2 b_j, i.e. M D G^2 + ridge D = B G^2; fit_core.py lines 115-117 solve this correctly, line 121 checks M G^2 D instead. selfcheck.py lines 19-35; runner_screen.py line 132.
findings.resolution: VERIFIED FIXED in the revised fit_core.py (SHA 34db25d270a9f99ef14a4fa291a3e3f7cbee2ce02725c1abd184fa1a3e671d44). Lines 121-122 now read lhs = (m.double() @ d64) * g2[None, :] + ridge * d64 and rhs = b.double() * g2[None, :], i.e. M D G^2 + ridge D = B G^2 with the gate scaling output columns on the right, exactly the system the eigen solve satisfies. Re-derived column j: minimizing sum_c ||(X_c D - R_c) G||_F^2/(S n_c Z) + ridge||D||_F^2 gives g_j^2 (sum_c X_c^T X_c/(S n_c Z)) d_j + ridge d_j = g_j^2 (sum_c X_c^T r_j/(S n_c Z)) = g_j^2 b_j; broadcast multiplication of (M@D) by g2[None,:] scales column j by g_j^2 -- orientation confirmed. The eigen solve (filt[k,j]=g_j^2/(g_j^2 mu_k+ridge); d64=V@(filt*(V^T B))) is UNCHANGED and remains correct. The residual is evaluated on the F64 solution against the same F32-accumulated Gram actually solved, a valid solve-quality certificate flowing into ridge_main_info/ridge_robust_info.
findings.recheck_evidence: Fresh independent pure-JS F64 replication (dense per-column Gaussian-elimination reference + Jacobi eigh with verified reconstruction ||V diag(mu) V^T - M|| ~ 1e-15; d=5, n=7, S=2, non-uniform g in [0.5,1.5], lam=1e-2): WELL-CONDITIONED case eigen-vs-dense rel=7.39e-16, NEW-formula normal residual=7.46e-16 (passes 1e-4 bound), OLD-formula residual=4.48e-1 (would fail); RANK-DEFICIENT case (rank-2 Gram, duplicated sources) eigen-vs-dense rel=3.15e-15, NEW residual=2.66e-16, OLD residual=3.48e-1, gram_numerical_rank=2. The fix is correct and the selfcheck abort path is cleared.

findings.item: The runtime gate-sharing assertion in _expensive_site checks only row [0] of the gate across CAL sources (torch.equal(pairs[source]['g'][0], g0)) and then uses that single row as the per-channel gate for the fit. It relies on R0 having verified the gate is per-channel (1,1,5120) and bitwise equal across all 9 sources at exactly these sites. This is safe given R0 (a per-token (31668,5120) gate would make cross-source row-0 equality fail loudly), but the assertion does not independently confirm all rows within a source are identical. Could be strengthened to assert per-channel structure at runtime.
findings.evidence: runner_screen.py lines 222-227; selector.py gate() lines 86-92; scope.json r0_verification.gate_identity (bitwise equal at high/0,4,19,34 step1 and low/4,19,34 step3).

findings.item: selfcheck.py exercises the ridge eigen-vs-dense solve only on a well-conditioned synthetic problem (d=5, n=7, 2 sources => full-rank 5x5 Gram). It does not test the severely rank-deficient/underdetermined regime (~500 rows for 5120 dims) that the real fit faces, nor the omega/numerical-rank diagnostics. The eigen algebra is exact regardless of conditioning so this is not a correctness gap, but test coverage of the identification diagnostics is thin. Note the existing normal-residual sub-check WOULD catch the blocking bug above once the job runs.
findings.evidence: selfcheck.py lines 11-35; scope.json limitations[1] (~114-137 matched rows/source, ~500 CAL rows for 5120x5120 D).
findings.resolution: VERIFIED FIXED in revised selfcheck.py (SHA e35b850000eafb218347c36cde95b8eb64c75c27c316e3daee9f6111d8c24bca), lines 44-57: a rank-deficient case (xr=randn(7,2)@randn(2,5) giving a rank-2 Gram in d=5, duplicated sources xs2=[xr,xr.clone()]) is checked against the same per-column F64 dense solve with rel<2e-4, normal-residual bound 1e-4, and gram_numerical_rank<=2. The _dense_ref helper (lines 7-21) solves g_j^2 M d_j + (lam/ZA) d_j = g_j^2 b_j per column with identical Z/ZA normalization and identical F32 Gram accumulation order -- mathematically the same normal equations as fit_core, a genuine independent reference. My independent JS replication confirms the case passes with the fixed code (eigen-vs-dense rel=3.15e-15, residual=2.66e-16, gram rank=2) and would have failed the residual bound under the old formula. The original well-conditioned case (seed 20261111, rel<2e-4, residual<1e-4), ICC zero-factor exactness, reuse-Y identity and zero-matrix BF16-replay checks all remain, and the new diagnostics are returned in the selfcheck dict. This exercises the mu~0 filter path the real ~500-row underdetermined fit hits.

checkpoint_numeric_recipe: Wan2.2-I2V-A14B-LightX2V-Distill-4step high/low safetensors (high SHA 39d3af74e46e59e989db5cc36f401e666f3ae77c7648eb55d3aff9fee47716fa, low SHA a3b8680affe2ab2e2121210a83ffa7d351f77da18191e57bb359d7839beba8a2), d=5120 m=13824, grid[21,29,52]=31668 tokens, BF16. Native FFN: z=addmm(b1,u,w1.T); h=GELU(z,approximate='tanh'); y=addmm(b2,h,w2.T) in BF16; TF32 off (cuda.matmul and cudnn), allow_bf16_reduced_precision_reduction=True. Math lift in FP32 (a.float(), x=u1.float()-u0.float(), pred=y0n+x@A). Deployed BF16 cache/gate replay (matches matrix_impl/fit_core.py replay_mse exactly): q0=u0@a, q1=u1@a (BF16), cache=BF16(y0.float()-q0.float()), base=BF16(q1.float()+cache.float()), gated=BF16(base.float()*g), target=BF16(y1.float()*g); error reductions in FP64. Q1 A=W1^T diag(alpha) W2^T exported F64->F32->BF16 RNE (deployed asset loaded as-is, NOT re-fit). FREE_RIDGE A_free=BF16(A_Q1+D_main), math lift uses unrounded FP32 sum. ICC svd_r512 two-residual: q1=z0-first(u0), q2=y0n-second(h0), hit=second(gelu(first(u1)+q1,tanh))+q2, evaluated as FP32-gate math lift. Small-M proxy: no full-M residual writeback. Ridge: shared Gram M=Sum_c X_c^T X_c/(S n_c Z), Z=mean_c||g*dy_c||^2/n_c+1e-12 (dy=F(U_t)-F(U_s)), ZA=||A_Q1||_F^2+1e-12, ridge=lambda/ZA, column j (g_j^2 M+ridge I)d_j=g_j^2 b_j via one eigh; lambda_main=1e-3, lambda_robust=1e-2 diagnostic only.
